comment: The scope statement describes what the architecture covers but not what it deliberately leaves to countries. Readers need to know which choices are architectural and which are political, because presenting a political choice as an architectural one is how national programmes lose legitimacy.

public.text: The scope statement describes what the architecture covers but not what it deliberately leaves to countries. Readers need to know which choices are architectural and which are political, because presenting a political choice as an architectural one is how national programmes lose legitimacy.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a short statement of what the guidance does not decide: the legal basis for processing and the consent or objection model; whether participation is voluntary or obligatory; who operates each component; how it is financed; and the balance between national and subnational authority. Stating this protects the guidance from being read as prescribing a centralised model, which is the reading that has defeated national programmes politically in more than one high-income country.
